title: Business Logic
description: Exploitation of application workflow flaws, transactional assumptions, race conditions, and economic/state-machine loopholes.

attacks.name: Price manipulation
attacks.desc: Modifying item price values in checkout requests (submitting negative numbers, zero, or fractional decimals) when backend handlers fail to validate prices against the database.
attacks.prevention: Calculate prices from trusted server-side product records and reject negative or unexpected totals.

attacks.name: Quantity abuse
attacks.desc: Submitting negative or zero quantities during e-commerce cart calculation to offset totals or manipulate financial ledger summaries.
attacks.prevention: Validate quantity ranges on the server and use safe numeric types that cannot wrap silently.

attacks.name: Coupon / discount abuse
attacks.desc: Applying single-use promotional discount codes repeatedly, stacking incompatible promotional codes, or bypassing minimum spending thresholds.
attacks.prevention: Bind coupons to eligibility rules, enforce usage limits atomically, and define stacking behavior explicitly.

attacks.name: Currency confusion
attacks.desc: Altering currency symbols or identifiers (e.g. paying 100 JPY instead of 100 USD) where the payment gateway processes the lower monetary value while the application fulfills the higher value order.
attacks.prevention: Normalize currency and minor units before calculation, and never trust a client-supplied currency conversion.

attacks.name: Race condition — double spend
attacks.desc: Sending concurrent parallel checkout or withdrawal requests within a microsecond window to withdraw balances multiple times before the database record updates.
attacks.prevention: Update balances atomically in one transaction or guarded operation, with idempotency for retries.

attacks.name: Race condition — double vote
attacks.desc: Exploiting non-atomic database checks by submitting concurrent voting requests, allowing users to register multiple votes before the user-has-voted flag is set.
attacks.prevention: Record each vote atomically against a unique voter/action key so concurrent requests cannot create duplicates.

attacks.name: TOCTOU
attacks.desc: Exploiting the timing gap between when a security permission or resource availability is verified and when the corresponding transaction or modification is committed.
attacks.prevention: Perform validation and state changes in one transaction or lock the affected resource across the operation.

attacks.name: Workflow step bypass
attacks.desc: Skipping mandatory verification or payment steps in multi-step onboarding, checkout, or KYC workflows by navigating directly to final confirmation endpoints.
attacks.prevention: Track workflow state on the server and reject steps submitted before their required predecessors.

attacks.name: Workflow reordering
attacks.desc: Executing workflow actions in an unexpected chronological order (such as applying a payment confirmation after clearing a cart) to induce invalid business state.
attacks.prevention: Require a valid server-side state transition for every step, independent of the order sent by the client.

attacks.name: Refund abuse
attacks.desc: Exploiting logic flaws in return and refund processes to trigger multiple refunds for a single purchase or receive refunds while retaining digital items.

attacks.name: Free trial abuse
attacks.desc: Repeatedly signing up for complimentary trial periods by altering email alias permutations, disposable card details, or machine fingerprints.

attacks.name: Rate limit bypass
attacks.desc: Circumventing API request limits by spoofing proxy headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP), varying endpoint casing, or distributing requests across IP rotations.

attacks.name: Inventory oversell
attacks.desc: Submitting simultaneous checkout requests to purchase scarce inventory items beyond available stock levels due to missing pessimistic/optimistic database locks.

attacks.name: Referral abuse
attacks.desc: Automating account registration pipelines to claim referral bonuses, signup credits, and affiliate rewards by referring synthetic user accounts.

attacks.name: Loyalty point abuse
attacks.desc: Exploiting rounding errors, cancellation loopholes, or order reversals where loyalty points earned on a purchase remain credited after the purchase is canceled.

attacks.name: Integer overflow in quantity
attacks.desc: Submitting integers exceeding 32-bit or 64-bit bounds in quantity fields to wrap calculations to negative numbers or small positive values, reducing invoice totals.

attacks.name: Object ID recycling
attacks.desc: Claiming newly generated objects that reuse deleted historical entity IDs, inadvertently inheriting permissions or historical audit associations from previous entities.

attacks.name: Multi-step form tampering
attacks.desc: Modifying parameters submitted in intermediate form steps to corrupt application state stored in user sessions or database draft records.

attacks.name: CAPTCHA reuse
attacks.desc: Replaying a single verified CAPTCHA solution across multiple subsequent business transactions when the server fails to invalidate the solution immediately after first verification.

attacks.name: Vote / reaction manipulation
attacks.desc: Artificially inflating product reviews, public polls, or post upvotes by rotating client session tokens or exploiting missing IP/account deduplication.

attacks.name: API pagination abuse
attacks.desc: Passing massive integer values in pagination limit parameters (e.g. ?limit=1000000) to force the backend to fetch and serialize huge datasets, degrading service performance.

attacks.name: Under-fetching / partial trust
attacks.desc: Relying on client-calculated tax rates, shipping fees, or line-item totals submitted in payloads rather than performing calculations authoritatively on the server.

attacks.name: Time-based logic abuse
attacks.desc: Exploiting business logic that relies on client-supplied timestamps or timezone data to manipulate time-sensitive discounts, auction bidding, or scheduled releases.

attacks.name: Rounding / float precision abuse
attacks.desc: Exploiting IEEE 754 floating-point inaccuracies or improper integer conversion in monetary calculations to skim fractional currency across numerous transactions.

attacks.name: Email/SMS cost abuse
attacks.desc: Automating requests to endpoints triggering international SMS or telephone OTP delivery, draining corporate communication budgets via premium-rate telephone numbers.
